Primary Care Progress Note
Date: 09/04/2026
Patient: Ivey Rice, 86-year-old female

Subjective:
Ms. Rice presents for routine follow-up. She reports no new complaints today.

Objective:
Vital signs are stable. Physical examination reveals no acute distress. Cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal exams are unremarkable.

Assessment:
Stable health status in an 86-year-old female with no new issues reported.

Plan:
Continue current management and routine monitoring. Encourage regular physical activity and balanced nutrition. Follow up in 6 months or sooner if new symptoms arise.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/17/2026
Patient: Ivey Rice, 86-year-old female

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/17/2026: acute osteoporotic L3 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

Impression:
There is an acute osteoporotic compression fracture at the L3 vertebral body, demonstrated by bone marrow edema on STIR sequences. No additional acute abnormalities are identified in the thoracolumbar spine.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Further management should be guided by the referring physician based on clinical findings.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/28/2026
Patient: Ivey Rice, 86-year-old female

History:
Back pain began 08/25/2026 after a fall from standing height, 5 weeks before this visit. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture.

Current Symptoms:
Pain NRS 7/10 despite 4 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis.

Assessment:
The patient presents with persistent pain related to a vertebral compression fracture sustained after a fall. No signs of systemic infection or discitis are present.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Continue current pain management and brace use. Consider interventional options based on follow-up evaluation.
